subject: Production latency & reserved-capacity shortfall — urgent exec alignment
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@shorebank.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.p@shorebank.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: High latency + failed transactions (prod) — seeing 5xx spike

Hi Sean / Marissa,

We started seeing a sustained latency spike and an uptick in 5xx errors beginning ~07:40 PT across our inference endpoints. This is directly impacting authorization flows (customers see "service unavailable" during peak checkout) — roughly 15% of requests failing and p95 latency jumping from ~180ms to 1.8s.

We rely on the Reserved capacity contract for predictable throughput; our dashboards show tokens queuing and a saturation signal pointing at the dedicated GPU pool serving our model. Attached is a short error snippet and the gate logs (prod-error-log-20261221.txt).

Please advise immediate mitigation steps and timeline to restore steady performance — this is affecting a live payment window for ShoreBank. If there's a way to route traffic to a fallback or authorize a short-term burst, we need that approved asap.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Engineering — ShoreBank
elena@shorebank.com

Attachments: prod-error-log-20261221.txt (text/plain, 48KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@shorebank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 08:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: High latency + failed transactions (prod) — seeing 5xx spike

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We can see the same signal in our telemetry: a steady queue depth increase on your reserved pool starting ~07:35, kernel-level saturation on the current quantized variant, and a small but material rise in KV-cache thrashing.

Immediate actions (in flight):
- Dev is standing up a capacity rebalancer to reclaim idle slots and accelerate prefix cache warm-up (ETA 20m).
- I’ve asked Infra to open the emergency burst gate to route up to 20% of incoming requests to a hosted-compatible variant to buy time (requires exec sign-off for billable burst or credit).
- Marissa: please confirm whether ShoreBank wants the hosted fallback enabled (it will change data/mode isolation briefly) or if we pursue an all-dedicated remediation.

Elena — we will prioritize a short-term remediation (fallback + rebalancer). I’ve looped in Vivek and Irene to get expedited authorization for a one-off burst allocation while engineering scales the dedicated pool.

Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@shorebank.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.p@shorebank.com>, Alex Howard <alex@cloudops-vendor.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: ShoreBank — proposed immediate remediation and procurement path

Team / Elena — quick update and ask from the account side.

What happened: sustained burst from ShoreBank during a regional payment peak saturated the dedicated pool serving their quantized 13B variant. The reserved commit was within contracted QPS, but the peak pattern (long-running batch inference + many short interactive calls) exceeded the runtime's effective concurrency headroom. That led to token queuing and higher error rates.

Proposed immediate plan (next 6 hours):
- Approve a one-time paid burst of 48 GPU-hours allocated to ShoreBank's pool (provides immediate headroom) — infra has a slot reservation flow that can attach to the account today.
- Enable hosted fallback for up to 30% of traffic while we rebalance (temporary; opt-in from ShoreBank required).
- Engineering to deploy a mid-term autoscale tweak: raise quick-scale threshold and pre-warm KV cache for ShoreBank's model; follow-up rollout by EOD.

Procurement / approvals: to enable the burst we need executive sign-off for either (A) one-off billable burst (invoice) or (B) apply a credit against ShoreBank's next invoice. We also need a procurement PO from ShoreBank if they opt for (A).

Attachments I am pushing to the thread: pool-usage-20261221.csv (hourly pool occupancy for the last 36 hours), sample latency graphs and an ops checklist.

Immediate asks from leaders:
- Vivek: authorization to grant the burst (we estimate ~$9K list value for 48 GPU-hours) or to approve a credit up to that amount.
- Irene: expedite infra provisioning and confirm the time to spin up two additional workers in the dedicated pool and the rollback plan.

Elena / Rajiv: which billing flow do you prefer (invoice vs credit)? If you prefer hosted fallback, reply "fallback:opt-in" and we will enable it once credits are agreed.

Marissa Cole
Account Lead — Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference
Attachments: pool-usage-20261221.csv (CSV, 12KB), ops-checklist.pdf (link provided in thread)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <elena@shorebank.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.p@shorebank.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 16:52:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: ShoreBank — proposed immediate remediation and procurement path

Thanks team — quick executive decision so we can move.

Decision: approve the one-time burst authorization of 48 GPU-hours to ShoreBank's dedicated tenancy. Charge will be applied as a billable burst against the account; Marissa to waive invoicing lead time and issue the emergency invoice with standard terms.

Conditions:
- Enable hosted fallback (up to 30%) only after ShoreBank confirms opt-in in writing. Elena, please confirm fallback:opt-in or fallback:decline. If decline, we will proceed with 100% dedicated remediation.
- Infra (Irene/Dev) to provision two additional workers and raise the autoscale quick-scale threshold now; monitor for 2 hours and roll back if we see increased tail latencies elsewhere.
- Post-incident: schedule an ops + product post-mortem with ShoreBank, include model quantization review and a recommendation for a small reserved uplift or burst-line in contract.

Marissa: please coordinate billing and cc finance. Sean / Irene / Dev — keep me posted every 30 minutes on progress. I will notify the executive sponsor at ShoreBank after we get Elena's confirmation.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
